The recovery accelerated as the quarter progressed. The funds attracted $172 million in July, $3.52 billion in August and $2.65 billion in September. Their largest daily inflow in August came on August 20, when the products added $606.3 million.

That period also brought a wave of liquidations in bearish leveraged positions. Short sellers were forced to buy Bitcoin to close their trades, adding to the upward move as the cryptocurrency gained more than $10,000 over several days.

ETF flows, however, do not provide a clean measure of directional institutional demand.

CoinShares Head of Research James Butterfill noted in the interview for Cointelegraph that some professional investors use BlackRock’s IBIT for basis trades, buying the ETF while shorting Bitcoin futures to capture the difference between spot and futures prices.

Corporate purchases provided another source of demand. Strategy resumed accumulating Bitcoin after a ten-week pause, purchasing 4,603 BTC for $369.7 million in late August.

Two subsequent acquisitions brought its holdings to 847,666 BTC by September 27. The next test is whether sustained spot and ETF demand can replace the temporary buying created by short liquidations.

“Aside from external macro numbers, I want to see sustained spot and ETF flows,” Nansen Senior Research Analyst Nicolai Sondergaard told Coindesk.

Treasury Yields Remain a Fourth-Quarter Constraint

The rally also followed the US Treasury’s decision to increase buybacks of longer-dated government debt, which pushed yields and the dollar lower in August.

Conditions subsequently tightened after the Federal Reserve raised interest rates in September and the ten-year Treasury yield climbed above 5%. Softer August inflation data later reduced expectations of another increase in October.

Nevertheless, elevated nominal and real yields remain a headwind by increasing the return available from lower-risk assets.

Near-term indicators are less uniformly bullish. Bitcoin remains in a bull market but is “showing signs of fatigue,” CryptoQuant Head of Research Julio Moreno wrote in a report cited by The Block. He placed initial support near the 365-day moving average at $80,000.

Other analysts identified $80,000–$82,000 as the main support area and $87,000–$88,000 as immediate resistance. Deribit data showed mixed short-term positioning, with traders alternating between demand for downside protection and exposure to a possible October rally.

Citi takes a more bullish view over a longer horizon. The bank raised its 12-month Bitcoin target from $82,000 to $113,000, citing renewed ETF demand, stronger crypto-market activity and a more supportive macroeconomic outlook. Its forecast assumes that investment flows continue at a slower but steadier pace.

The fourth-quarter outlook will depend on whether sustained ETF and spot demand can offset higher yields once the short-covering impulse fades.

title: Another Trump memecoin dinner advertised for token's top investors
summary: The company managing the memecoin calls the November event the "most exclusive dinner in the world."
content:
Oct 1, 2026, 2:45 p.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • President Donald Trump’s memecoin investors will get another chance to have dinner with the leader of the U.S. executive branch, with the token managers marketing another “gala dinner” for November.
  • Though Trump is set to attend the event at his Washington, D.C,-area club, the three “legends” advertised on the website haven’t yet been announced.
  • Similar events have drawn criticism from Democratic lawmakers as brash corruption that grants political connection to those investing the most money.

Investors in Donald Trump's memecoin are getting another shot at being in a room with the U.S. president, the third such event following others that drew criticism from Democratic lawmakers as an openly corrupt selling of the White House.

The top 185 registered investors in $TRUMP will be invited through the doors of his Trump National private club in Washington, D.C., on November 22, according to the website that manages $TRUMP events. The VIP status — determined by investor engagement in the token — will be locked on November 12, the organization said.

When the "gala dinner" was announced, the price of the coin popped up about 10% to $2.25 before sinking again near the level it's been at in recent days — still a small fraction of the all-time high of around $74.

The event is being billed as the "most exclusive dinner in the world," and is advertising that three other "legends" will join the president, though none have yet been identified.

One thing is for sure, according to the club: "No attendees will be granted a private meet & greet with the President."

That had been a point of disappointment for some participants in past events: While Trump briefly appeared, they didn't get a chance to meet him.

Since his memecoin's launch in the days before he took office again, investors have lost billions of dollars, and those losses have occupied the spotlight during the recent debates over the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act — the crypto market structure bill in the Senate. With Trump's crypto empire in mind, Democratic lawmakers had insisted that the bill limit the digital asset ties of senior government officials, but that provision could never be worked out, and the bill failed to advance last month.

Trump had said he was willing to concede on some of the requests and potentially place his crypto holdings in a blind trust or divest them, but the deal fell apart when the bill failed.

The first Trump memecoin event was also at Trump's Washington-era golf club, and protesters — including congressional Democrats — gathered outside to accuse the president of corruption as unidentified guests gathered.

In April, Trump held a related conference at Mar-a-Lago in Florida for memecoin holders, at which former champion boxer Mike Tyson appeared.

This time, the top "VIPs" will be given gifts, including a commemorative poster and "TRUMP fragrance." The website's tally of current registrants shows that the top investors seeking invitations each hold hundreds of thousands of coins.

title: 50,000 Europeans call on EU to ease stablecoin rewards restrictions in MiCA review
summary: A 50,000-letter campaign is pressing Brussels to rethink stablecoin rewards as EU central banks seek broader changes to MiCA’s stablecoin rules.
content:
More than 50,000 Europeans have urged the European Commission to loosen restrictions on stablecoin rewards as part of its review of the bloc’s Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) framework, according to crypto advocacy group Stand With Crypto EU.

The campaign came as the Commission closed its MiCA review consultation on Wednesday, with Stand With Crypto EU pushing for regulated stablecoin providers to be allowed to offer incentives including cashback, loyalty benefits and fee reductions.

The group said more than 50,000 supporters wrote to the Commission during the consultation, while more than 126,000 people have separately signed its petition calling for a more permissive EU approach to stablecoins.

Stand With Crypto EU campaign vehicle outside the European Parliament in Brussels, Belgium. Source: Stand With Crypto EU

MiCA prohibits issuers and crypto service providers from paying interest on stablecoins, a restriction Stand With Crypto argues puts the products at a disadvantage to bank deposits and other e-money products that can offer benefits to customers.

Stand With Crypto said the campaign generated more than six times the 8,221 responses submitted to the European Central Bank’s (ECB) digital euro consultation and far exceeded the 198 responses received during the Commission’s 2020 consultation on crypto rules.

Stand With Crypto calls for EU to compete with US

“We are calling on the Commission to use the MiCA review to allow regulated stablecoins to offer rewards to holders,” Stand With Crypto EU general manager Harry Pearce Gould told Cointelegraph.

Asked whether Europe should look to regulatory models outside the EU, Pearce Gould pointed to the US:

The US has made a clear choice to back stablecoins as the settlement layer for tokenisation. Europe doesn’t need to copy that, but it does need to compete with it.

He added that allowing rewards could help euro-denominated stablecoins gain adoption and compete with dollar stablecoins.

“Strong euro stablecoins matter for the euro’s global standing and the EU’s payment sovereignty,” he said.

Related: Binance’s EU services face scrutiny over licensing exemption: Report

EU central banks seek changes to stablecoin rules

The campaign comes as European central banks are pushing for broader changes to MiCA’s treatment of stablecoins.

In a Sept. 22 response to the European Commission’s MiCA review, the European System of Central Banks (ESCB) called for the existing prohibition on stablecoin interest to extend to lending, borrowing and staking arrangements that generate yield.

The ESCB also proposed replacing MiCA requirements that stablecoin issuers hold a minimum share of their reserves in bank deposits with liquidity thresholds. The central banks argued that the existing rules could strain lenders if a stablecoin run forced an issuer to rapidly withdraw deposits.

The ECB has separately highlighted a potential liquidity mismatch, noting in June that stablecoins settle around the clock while their reserve assets may still operate on traditional settlement timelines.

Source: European Central Bank

The proposals come amid broader concerns from the ECB over stablecoins’ potential impact on financial stability.

In May, ECB President Christine Lagarde warned that a shift of deposits from banks into stablecoins could weaken bank lending and monetary policy transmission, while arguing that Europe should instead prioritize tokenized financial infrastructure anchored by central bank money.

title: Lowest Fee Bitcoin ATMs Announces Launch of More Than 400 ATMs Nationwide

Las Vegas, NV, October 1st, 2026, Chainwire

Lowest Fee Bitcoin ATMs announced the launch of more than 400 cryptocurrency ATMs across the United States. The machines allow customers to purchase Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT and USDC with cash at a stated flat 5% fee. Customers can also pre-register online before visiting an ATM.

Lowest Fee Bitcoin ATMs, a new nationwide low-fee Bitcoin ATM operator, launched today with an initial rollout of more than 400 Bitcoin ATMs across the United States, a footprint that places it amongst the largest Bitcoin ATM operators in the country on its first day. It also launched with a name that does most of the marketing department’s job for it. The brand charges a flat 5% Bitcoin ATM fee to buy Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT or USDC with cash, displays the fee and exchange rate on screen before the customer confirms, and, as of today, lets first-time customers register online in about two minutes so they can skip onboarding at the machine entirely.

400+ Bitcoin ATM locations on day one

Most Bitcoin ATM operators in the U.S. run a few dozen machines. Lowest Fee Bitcoin ATMs opens with more than 400 Bitcoin ATM locations in the convenience stores, gas stations and shopping centers people already visit, with machines in Florida, California, Arizona and Texas among other states, as the first phase of a larger rollout.

“Four hundred machines is not a pilot. It’s a network,” said Quincy Mathis, Operations Manager at Lowest Fee Bitcoin ATMs. “We wanted to be one of the biggest Bitcoin ATM operators in the country on the day we opened, because a low fee only matters if there’s a machine near you. This is phase one.”

Buy Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT and USDC with cash: coins, limits and one fee

Every Lowest Fee Bitcoin ATM sells Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), Tether (USDT) and USD Coin (USDC) for cash, all at the same 5% fee, all sent directly to the customer’s own wallet. No bank account or credit card is needed. The machines are non-custodial: the company never holds customer funds.

Bitcoin ATM daily limits are set by verification tier:

  • Tier 1, phone number only: up to $2,000 per day
  • Tier 2, government ID and Tax ID: up to $50,000 per day

Bitcoin ATM fees compared: what $1,000 buys

The typical Bitcoin ATM in the United States charges roughly 12% to 15% to buy, and some of the largest national brands charge 20% or more. Here is what that looks like when a customer walks up with $1,000 in cash:

Illustrative, based on posted percentage fees only and before exchange rate. Many operators add an exchange-rate markup on top of the posted fee; Lowest Fee Bitcoin ATMs shows both the fee and the rate on screen before a transaction is confirmed. Industry figures reflect publicly reported U.S. Bitcoin ATM fee ranges. See how the Bitcoin ATM fees compare.

At a 20% machine, one dollar in every five never becomes crypto. At Lowest Fee Bitcoin ATMs, it’s one in twenty. The name is not subtle; neither is a 20% fee.

“We wanted a rate people can look at on the receipt and feel good about, not one they have to make peace with,” said Quincy Mathis. “Five percent, shown up front, with the exchange rate right next to it. That’s the whole pitch.”

Stablecoin ATMs are becoming the way people send money overseas

A growing share of customers are using the machines as USDT and USDC ATMs, buying dollar pegged stable coins to send money to family and friends overseas and to pay suppliers and contractors abroad. A customer inserts cash, the stable coins arrive in the recipient’s wallet within minutes, and the recipient holds dollars they can keep or cash out locally. No wire counter, no multi-day wait, and no bank account needed to send.

That makes the fee gap matter more, not less. Someone sending $1,000 home once a month pays about $600 a year in fees at a 5% machine, $1,440 to $1,800 at a typical machine, and $2,400 at a 20% machine. The difference is real money to the people who can least afford to lose it, which is why low fees matter most to remittance customers.

“The people using stable coins to support family abroad are exactly the people who shouldn’t be paying 20% for the privilege,” said Quincy Mathis.

How to use a Bitcoin ATM: four steps, under two minutes, now with online pre-registration

New with today’s launch is online Bitcoin ATM pre-registration. First-time customers can pre-register online before they ever visit a machine, so the first visit is as fast as the tenth. At any of the 400+ machines, they simply enter their phone number.

  1. Register online, once. About two minutes on a phone.
  2. Walk up and enter your phone number. The machine recognizes you. No paperwork at the kiosk.
  3. Pick a coin, scan your wallet, insert cash. Scan your wallet’s QR code and feed in the bills.
  4. Check the screen and confirm. The fee and exchange rate are displayed before you press anything. Crypto lands in your wallet within minutes.

Customers who would rather register at the machine still can. It just takes a little longer, and the company would like to gently point out that it no longer has to. A full walkthrough of how a Bitcoin ATM works is on the company’s website.

Compliance, briefly

Lowest Fee Bitcoin ATMs is a FinCEN-registered money services business, and every machine operates in compliance with federal and state regulations. Customer data is encrypted, and transactions are non-custodial and irreversible. No government agency, bank, utility or tech-support line will ever ask anyone to pay them at a Bitcoin ATM; if someone does, it is a scam. Common questions are answered in the company’s Bitcoin ATM FAQ.

Find a low-fee Bitcoin ATM near you

Lowest Fee Bitcoin ATMs are live now at 400+ locations across the United States, with further phases of the rollout to follow. Customers can find a Bitcoin ATM near them and pre-register at lowestfeebitcoinatms.com. New customers can use code LOWEST at the machine for 20% off the transaction fee, which brings the fee on that $1,000 transaction down to $40.

Key Takeaways:

  • From its mere 0.1% of the world’s major markets, it is his estimation that this represents a $160 billion opportunity.
  • Strategy and Strive is developing separate products with the same base of Bitcoin capital.

Bitcoin treasury companies don’t have to bicker with one another as a form of direct zero-sum game, according to Michael Saylor.

In a recent post, the Strategy executive chairman argued that firms such as Strategy and Strive can attract different investors while helping expand the broader market for Bitcoin-linked capital, credit and equity products.

  • Saylor Sees a $160B Opportunity Outside Crypto
  • Bitcoin Connects Strategy and Strive
    • More Digital Credit Issuers Could Expand the Market
    • Strive Already Holds $50M of Strategy’s STRC

Saylor Sees a $160B Opportunity Outside Crypto

Saylor begins his discussion with the dimensions of traditional capital markets. Global equity market capitalization reached about $157.8 trillion at the end of 2025, while global fixed-income debt stood at roughly $160.7 trillion.

A 0.1% allocation from both markets would vary from about $160 billion, the amount Saylor demonstrated was still a tiny portion of the traditional finance treasury when compared to Bitcoin.

According to his plan, Bitcoin is Digital Capital, preferred securities like STRC, SATA are Digital Credit, and MSTR, ASST are Digital Equity. Decisions vary among these groups based on investors’ goals ranging from equity exposure to income to capital appreciation.

Read More: Michael Saylor Sparks Fresh Bitcoin Buy Buzz as Strategy Nears $62B BTC Stockpile

Bitcoin Connects Strategy and Strive

Both Strategy and Strive issue their own securities and make their own financing choices; however, Bitcoin is a central balance-sheet asset.

If one company raises capital and purchases Bitcoin, then a stronger demand for Bitcoin can benefit other companies which own BTC indirectly, Saylor suggests.

But that’s not all that it takes to drive Bitcoin up. However, price continues to be influenced by the global market demand. Even if they are rivals seeking investors’ dollars, he argues, treasury companies are aligned through exposure to the same underlying asset.

More Digital Credit Issuers Could Expand the Market

Saylor also thinks that there’s room for other, reliable credit issues to get up and clarify the investment of credit products backed by Bitcoin. The more security, the more of its trading history, its research coverage and degree of institutional familiarity.

As investors reach a higher comfort level in assessing products like STRC and SATA, over time they could settle for lower risk premiums. That might make financing more favorable for those with decent balance sheets and management.

Saylor reaffirmed that no Bitcoin per se tests out offering any coupon income. There is no risk-reward alignment in Bitcoin’s long-term performance and financing costs, only execution and market conditions and capital management.

Read More: Strategy Sells Bitcoin for First Time Since 2022 While Still Holding 843,706 BTC

Strive Already Holds $50M of Strategy’s STRC

The relationship between Strategy and Strive is already more than theoretical. In March 2026, one Bitcoin-focused company Strive made a $50 million investment to buy STRC from strategy, which was the issuer’s credit product.

Saylor sees this kind of overlap as proof that Bitcoin treasury companies can exist in the same eco-system as competition and customers.

His broader thesis is that Digital Capital, Digital Credit and Digital Equity can reinforce one another by bringing more investors, liquidity and financial products into the Bitcoin market.

title: Illinois will postpone implementation of crypto tax following lawsuit
summary: State officials agreed to delay the 0.2% crypto tax for six months after lawsuits and industry pushback claimed the bill was rushed through the legislature.
content:
Crypto advocacy organizations behind a lawsuit opposing Illinois’ Digital Asset Tax reported that state officials agreed to delay implementation by six months.

In a Thursday filing in the circuit court of Sangamon County, Illinois, the crypto and blockchain advocacy group Digital Chamber said that Illinois would postpone a 0.2% tax on digital assets from Jan. 1 to July 1, 2027. The organization sued Illinois Attorney General Kwame Raoul and the Department of Revenue official David Harris in July, claiming the tax had been “slipped into the state’s budget” without debate or public feedback.

“The Parties stipulate that continuing the Tax’s effective date from January 1, 2027 until July 1, 2027 will permit orderly briefing and adjudication of the underlying legal questions without prejudicing any Party’s rights, claims, or defenses on the merits,” the filing said.

Source: Digital Chamber

The digital asset tax was included in a senate bill as part of the Illinois state budget for the fiscal year 2027, signed into law by Governor JB Pritzker in June. Under the legislation, crypto brokers would have been required to impose a 0.2% tax or face potential prison time and fines starting on Jan. 1.

Related: Illinois draft crypto tax rules detail DeFi, stablecoin treatment

Digital Chamber CEO Cody Carbone called the delay a “major win” for the crypto industry but said that the organization would continue to attempt to overturn the tax in court.

“[A] delay is not a repeal,” said Carbone. “The job isn’t done, and we won’t stop until this tax is struck down for good.”

Other lawsuits likely still pending in state court

The Digital Chamber’s lawsuit was separate from legal actions taken by the Crypto Council for Innovation (CCI) and Blockchain Association (BA) in August. The two trade associations argued against the crypto tax on constitutional grounds, later seeking to block its Jan. 1 implementation with a preliminary injunction.

As of Thursday, the status of the CCI and BA lawsuit was unclear given the agreement for a six-month delay. Cointelegraph contacted the organizations for comment but did not receive an immediate response.

title: Peter Todd Joins MARA to Lead Private Mempool Slipstream
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Peter Todd Joins MARA to Lead Private Mempool Slipstream
Bitcoin O.G. Peter Todd has joined the MARA Foundation as lead maintainer of Slipstream, the miner’s private Bitcoin mempool service.  Announced by the foundation on Thursday, the new role will see Todd responsible for develo...
content:
Bitcoin O.G. Peter Todd has joined the MARA Foundation as lead maintainer of Slipstream, the miner’s private Bitcoin mempool service. 

Announced by the foundation on Thursday, the new role will see Todd responsible for developing and running the service.

Slipstream lets users send bitcoin transactions straight to MARA Pool, the company’s mining pool, without going through Bitcoin’s public peer-to-peer network. It was useful after hackers exploited Coldcard hardware wallets in July, stealing over $115 million in user funds. 

Because transactions sent through Slipstream stay private until they’re confirmed in a block, the service helps to keep key information hidden before confirmation — protecting exposure of their public keys. 

“I most look forward to seeing what’s possible on Bitcoin — using Slipstream as a proving ground for experimental development and protocol innovation,” Todd said. 

Todd added: “Working with Slipstream is a natural complement to my work on Libre Relay, and my mempool policy work more broadly. I’ve always believed that Bitcoin is better when we design protocols with economic demand in mind. This is also a good opportunity to build bridges between Bitcoin Core developers and miners.”

MARA’s Slipstream first drew attention in 2024 for publishing large Ordinals inscriptions. More recently it has been used for research projects like Quantum Safe Bitcoin and Binohash, a way to emulate covenants without a soft fork.

Todd is a longtime Bitcoin Core contributor, who co-authored BIP 125 (replace-by-fee), created OpenTimestamps, and in 2024 launched Libre Relay, a Bitcoin Core fork with looser relay rules for non-standard transactions. 

He argues that mempool policy should follow what the market wants miners to mine, rather than restrict how people use Bitcoin.

Key Takeaways:

  • According to the company, there is presently no risk to the MetaMask wallets.
  • As a precaution, Ethereum validators affected are in the process of being exited.

MetaMask has announced that it has started rolling out the removal of impacted Ethereum validators due to a security incident impacting part of its infrastructure.

Security Update: We are responding to a security incident affecting part of our infrastructure.

At this time, we have identified no immediate threat to MetaMask wallets.

As a precaution, we are proactively exiting affected validators within our non-custodial staking operations,…

— MetaMask 🦊 (@MetaMask) September 30, 2026

The wallet provider said the problem is under investigation and will be fixed through relationship work done in collaboration with outside service providers and security advisors, and emphasized that users are not immediately at risk for MetaMask wallets.

  • MetaMask Takes Validators Offline After Security Incident
  • Wallet Users Face No Immediate Threat
    • Lido Validators Enter Exit Process
    • Ethereum Re-Entry Could Take Up to 45 Days

MetaMask Takes Validators Offline After Security Incident

MetaMask has yet to reveal the nature, cause or extent of the event. The issue is impacting some of its infrastructure and the company is working to contain and address the issue internally, it said.

To safeguard itself, MetaMask is scaling down its validators of its non-custodial staking service.

The change should help lower possible risk of exposure until the investigation concludes but so far, the company hasn’t said that any funds or wallet users are being compromised.

MetaMask’s model is also non-custodial, which it noted. Withdrawal keys for the assets they stake are not managed by the company.

Read More: MetaMask Splits From Consensys as 100M-Download Wallet Targets Open Money

Wallet Users Face No Immediate Threat

MetaMask specifically separated the infrastructure incident from its wallet product.

There is a significant distinction, however, in that the company did not detect any apparent immediate issue with wallets in their use of MetaMask it says, which is important because of the number of people using wallets and the position of the wallet in the Ethereum ecosystem.

The company hasn’t made any user movements, wallet or other emergency measure requirements. MetaMask stated it will monitor the situation and share more additional information if appropriate.

Lido Validators Enter Exit Process

MetaMask Staking validators also saw the impact from the security measures taken by the Lido protocol. MetaMask began proactively taking measures with its operated validators regarding Ethereum, such as initiating withdrawals, said Lido.

Lido provided timeline updates on other affected validators, stating that the final affected validators will exit by October 7, 2021. ETH that is taken off the affected validators is not presumed to be immediately returned to the protocol, but a phase where it is slowly made available to the network is assumed.

Ethereum Re-Entry Could Take Up to 45 Days

Once they have withdrawn, the funds then have to pass through the Ethereum process of validators entering, and their funds being withdrawn. Since the current validator entry queue, Lido hopes up to 45 days for the full withdrawal and re-entry process.

This does not mean the report of a lost ETH has been made. Rather, it represents the dynamics of withdrawing validators from the Ethereum protocol to withdraw later on the validators.

MetaMask has so far resolved to view the validator exits as a precautionary security feature, not a security flaw affecting the user’s wallets or their ability to withdraw funds.

title: Base Cobalt Goes Live With Conditional Trades and New B20 Controls for Tokenized Assets
summary:
Key Takeaways: The newest Cobalt upgrade by Base has been activated on the mainnet. Traders can send orders which will only be filled when certain criteria are fulfilled. B20 new
The post Base Cobalt Goes Live With Conditional Trades and New B20 Controls for Tokenized Assets appeared first on Crypto...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • The newest Cobalt upgrade by Base has been activated on the mainnet.
  • Traders can send orders which will only be filled when certain criteria are fulfilled.
  • B20 new compliance tools, corporate-action and asset-control tools.

Base has launched its third major network upgrade, Cobalt, which provides increased control over transaction execution, as well as additional growth opportunities for the B20 token standard in onchain asset issuance.

The upgrade addresses two aspects: the new advanced trade functionality via validity transactions, and enhanced support for Foundation’s tokenized finance assets.

  • Base Adds Conditional Transactions for Advanced Traders
  • Transactions Can Stay Private Until Inclusion
    • B20 Gets New Controls for Tokenized Assets
    • Base Targets 200ms Blocks in Upcoming Upgrades

Base Adds Conditional Transactions for Advanced Traders

Cobalt introduces Validity Transactions, allowing users to sign and submit a transaction before its execution conditions are satisfied. Instead of repeatedly monitoring the market and resubmitting orders, a trader can specify conditions such as an asset price threshold and a block-number deadline.

Base then checks what their requirements are as new blocks come in. The transaction is eligible for inclusion once all of the conditions have been met.

A trader, for instance, can place a swap that only takes place when a token sees 4,000 USDC before a particular block. In the case of the price condition not being met before the deadline, no transaction will be added. Users must still select the transaction and define both the conditions and the transaction. They do not trade on Base.

Read More: Coinbase Targets $24/5 Stock Perps in First U.S. Push for Single-Stock Crypto Futures

Transactions Can Stay Private Until Inclusion

Validity Transactions can also be kept private until they get to the onchain. This enables the sophisticated traders to have more control on when they want to expose their orders and will lessen the need for continuously polling blockchain state.

It will now be provided via Base’s new Transaction API and will be suitable for strategies that rely on particular timings or onchain conditions.

B20 Gets New Controls for Tokenized Assets

Cobalt also launches B20, a native token standard for stablecoins, tokenized real-world assets and fungible assets. One new feature, Composite Policies, enables issuers to create AND and OR combinations based on various compliance rules.

For instance, a tokenized fund may need a recipient to complete KYC and accreditation requirements and may use separate providers to perform sanctions screening.

Also new on Cobalt are scheduled multiplier changes. Issuers can program changes used for corporate actions such as stock splits without minting or burning tokens or changing the underlying raw balance.

An additional feature is seizeWithMemo, which allows for transferring balances with seizure functionality since it is enabled for a token. Can be an onchain note that explains what action is being taken as part of the transfer.

This does not cause a Base to move into itself. Whether the function is enabled and who can use it will be determined by the issuer.

Base Targets 200ms Blocks in Upcoming Upgrades

Cobalt is within a longer technological path regarding trading, financing, and payments through tokens. Base will target even shorter block times (200 milliseconds) and reassert its current guarantees on organization.

The network will also be supporting protocol-level smart accounts and gas sponsorship and transaction batching, among other EVM enhancements.

For asset issuers, traders and developers, the Cobalt is moving Base closer towards an infrastructure that supports programmable financial products instead of just token transfers.

The post Bloomberg Launches $300B Stablecoin Dashboard With Hourly Onchain Data on Terminal appeared fir...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Allium has now provided Bloomberg Terminal with hourly stablecoin data.
  • The dashboard includes over 98% of the stablecoin market.
  • Users can follow the movement of supply and mints, burns and transfers and the activity on the different blockchains.

Bloomberg is releasing a new stablecoin dashboard on the Bloomberg Terminal, making it possible to bring onchain market data right into the workflow of institutional investors.

It’s driven by blockchain data provider Allium and is backed by a stablecoin supply of over $300 billion.

  • Bloomberg Terminal Adds Stablecoin Market Tracking
  • Users Can Break Down Activity by Blockchain
    • Stablecoin Supply Tops $300B
    • Bloomberg Expands Its Onchain Data Push

Bloomberg Terminal Adds Stablecoin Market Tracking

The new dashboard will be offered via RWAS <GO> and morphs stablecoin analytics with BWFX’s current fixed-income, foreign exchange and money-market offerings.

It includes all stablecoin that have a circulation above $100 million which is more than 98% of the total market. Bloomberg also offers selected smaller assets, and stablecoins that are based on other currencies or commodities than the U.S. dollar.

Users can use circular supply, token issuance, burns, transfer volume and velocity to compare the assets. Current information will be updated once an hour and historical information will be updated a day-fresh.

Read More: South Korea Targets 2027 Tokenized Securities Launch with Stablecoin Settlement Vision

Users Can Break Down Activity by Blockchain

The dashboard provides more insight into the performance of select stablecoins on various blockchains. Users can also quickly switch between an asset-level and blockchain-level view, to help them understand where the issuance and transfers are happening.

The assets can also be sorted by peg, such as the fiat currencies, commodities or any other stablecoins. This allows investors to have a solid understanding of the liquidity of the stablecoins in question rather than crossing multiple blockchain explorers and analytics sites.

Stablecoin Supply Tops $300B

Stablecoins have emerged as a key component of the crypto market infrastructure, having a circulatory supply of over $300 billion.

Now they are not just involved in crypto trading. Stablecoins are gaining traction as a means of settlement, for cross-border payments, and to transfer cash in tokenized financial systems.

They also now closely follow traditional markets, as large issuers have substantial quantities of short-dated U.S. government paper as their reserve assets.

Bloomberg’s new product puts that activity on a platform utilized by banks, asset management companies and institutional trading desks.

Read More: Coinbase and Spiko Unlock 24/7 Stablecoin Access to Europe’s Regulated UCITS Funds

Bloomberg Expands Its Onchain Data Push

The stablecoin dashboard expands upon Bloomberg’s long-standing crypto expansion efforts.

Since 2014, Bitcoin pricing has been available at the Terminal, and Bloomberg now offers pricing, benchmarks and identifiers and reference data for over 50 institutional-relevant cryptocurrencies.

The firm has also created a portfolio level measure of direct and indirect crypto exposure.

Its collaboration with Allium pushes that strategy further by adding blockchain-native transaction data to the same environment institutions already use for traditional markets.

More recently though, Bloomberg has been pushing its oar into the tokenized-market space with other data partnerships, as part of a generica push for DeFi and traditional-capital market insights to combine in a single institutional workflow.

title: Zcash (ZEC) Price Prediction: Whale Accumulation and ETF Outflows Put ZEC at a Critical Crossroads Around $1,400
summary: Zcash (ZEC) is consolidating around $1,400 after a sharp September rally, with whale accumulation supporting the market while weakening ETF flows and bearish momentum indicators introduce fresh uncertainty.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: ZEC

Zcash (ZEC) is consolidating around $1,400 after a sharp September rally, with whale accumulation supporting the market while weakening ETF flows and bearish momentum indicators introduce fresh uncertainty.

The Zcash price reached a September high near $1,687 before retreating toward the $1,400 area. Historical price data shows the token closing near $1,414 on September 30 after trading as low as roughly $1,362 during the session.

The latest move has created a mixed setup for the Zcash price prediction. Large wallet withdrawals suggest continued interest from some holders, while technical indicators and recent ETF redemptions point to a market that is still digesting its rapid advance.

ZEC Price Holds Around $1,400 as Momentum Cools

ZEC has entered a consolidation phase following one of its strongest rallies of 2026. After climbing above $1,600 in late September, the token suffered a series of pullbacks and briefly moved toward the $1,360-$1,400 region.

ZEC’s 1H chart shows a rising parallel channel following the late-September selloff, suggesting potential bearish consolidation as momentum resets. Source: @XRPathologist via X

An analysis posted by @XRPathologist identifies a rising parallel channel on the 1-hour chart. The structure developed after the late-September selloff, with the price recovering gradually inside the channel rather than immediately reclaiming its previous highs.

The setup is being viewed as a potential bearish consolidation pattern. In this structure, price can continue moving higher while underlying momentum weakens.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) has also shown bearish divergence across multiple timeframes, according to the analysis. That occurs when price attempts to hold or extend gains while momentum indicators fail to confirm the move.

The analyst highlighted the two channel boundaries as important technical reference points. A break above the upper rail would weaken the bearish interpretation, while a move below the lower boundary could increase the risk of another decline.

This leaves the $1,400 area as an important near-term level for the Zcash price prediction, particularly after the recent correction.

Zcash Whales Withdraw $28 Million From Exchanges

While the short-term chart has become less decisive, on-chain activity is providing a different signal.

Lookonchain reported that two wallets believed to be linked to the same whale withdrew a combined 24,706 ZEC from Binance and Gate during the past month. The transfers were valued at approximately $28.17 million at an average price of $1,140 per ZEC.

Two wallets believed to be linked to the same whale withdrew 24,706 ZEC worth $28.17 million from Binance and Gate over the past month, averaging $1,140 per ZEC. Source: @lookonchain via X

The wallets identified in the report are t1ggpKAwzURp8SToryGH1ELeqTfHDNuttw7 and t1dB4hr2MdtjJ2mBnWqYyTRXjte6mTQ3XkN. Arkham-linked transaction data cited by Lookonchain shows repeated movements from exchange wallets into these addresses.

Lookonchain described the activity as whale accumulation despite the decline in ZEC’s price.

Exchange withdrawals can reduce the amount of an asset immediately available for trading, but they do not by themselves prove that the coins will be held for the long term. Wallet ownership is also not independently confirmed in the available data.

Still, the timing is notable. The withdrawals occurred as ZEC moved lower from its September peak, indicating that at least some large holders were moving coins away from exchanges during the correction.

Zcash ETF Flows Reverse After Strong Start

Institutional exposure through exchange-traded products has been another major factor behind ZEC’s 2026 rally.

Grayscale’s Zcash ETF, trading under the ticker ZCSH, began trading on NYSE Arca on August 25. Grayscale described it as the first exchange-traded product to offer spot exposure to ZEC.

The fund initially attracted substantial demand. By September 18, ZCSH had accumulated more than $233 million in inflows and had grown to nearly $890 million in net assets, according to The Block.

Grayscale ETF clients sold $30.25 million in ZEC, according to WhaleInsider on October 1, 2026. Source: @WhaleInsider via X

Grayscale also completed a planned 3-for-1 forward share split, with split-adjusted trading beginning on September 30. The split changed the number of shares and their individual price without changing the underlying value of the fund.

However, ETF momentum weakened toward the end of September. Reported U.S. spot Zcash ETF flows were flat for three consecutive sessions from September 23 through September 25, followed by an $8.12 million net outflow on September 28.

The trend became more significant on September 30, when U.S. spot Zcash ETFs reportedly recorded a $30.25 million net outflow. ZCSH accounted for the reported withdrawal, while cumulative net inflows remained positive at roughly $268 million.

The outflow does not necessarily mean that individual ETF clients broadly abandoned ZEC. ETF flow data measures net creations and redemptions, so it is better interpreted as a change in fund demand rather than proof of the intentions of every investor.

Despite the recent reversal, the scale of the fund remains substantial. ZCSH had previously crossed $500 million in assets within two weeks of its launch, while Grayscale said cumulative inflows had exceeded $70 million in addition to a $100 million investment from DCG International Investments.

Privacy Demand Keeps Zcash in Focus

The longer-term narrative around Zcash remains closely tied to financial privacy.

Grayscale Head of Research Zach Pandl recently highlighted the scale of ZEC’s rise over the past year, noting that its price had increased from roughly $60 to around $1,500. He also said Zcash’s market capitalization had expanded from less than 0.1% of Bitcoin’s market cap to about 1.5%.

Grayscale’s Zach Pandl noted that Zcash rose from about $60 to $1,500 over the past year, while its market-cap share of Bitcoin increased from below 0.1% to 1.5%. Source: @crypto_banter via X

Pandl pointed to growing demand for privacy-preserving technology as a factor that could support further adoption. Zcash uses zk-SNARK technology to allow users to shield transaction information while maintaining network verification.

That privacy functionality differentiates Zcash from many other digital assets and has become more relevant as institutional and individual users increasingly examine how transaction information is exposed across blockchain networks.

The shift in Zcash’s market position has been substantial. However, the recent price correction shows that strong long-term narratives do not eliminate short-term volatility.

ZEC Price Prediction: Key Levels to Watch

The $1,400 region has become an important reference point following the September correction. ZEC’s ability to stabilize around this area could determine whether the current consolidation develops into another recovery attempt or evolves into a deeper retracement.

Zcash (ZEC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

On the upside, a sustained move through the upper boundary of the short-term rising channel would weaken the bearish technical setup identified by @XRPathologist. A recovery toward the September highs would then bring the $1,600-$1,700 area back into focus.

On the downside, a break below the lower channel boundary would indicate that the current rebound is losing structure. The recent low around $1,360 provides another nearby reference from the latest correction. Historical data shows that ZEC traded down to approximately $1,362 on September 29 before recovering.

The conflicting signals make the current Zcash price prediction particularly sensitive to confirmation. Whale withdrawals and the broader expansion of ZCSH provide evidence of continued interest in ZEC, while bearish RSI divergence and renewed ETF outflows point to weaker short-term momentum.

For now, the $1,400 area remains a key level as traders assess whether Zcash can stabilize after its September rally or continue correcting from its recent highs.

title: 21X Group Announces Collaboration with Circle as it joins Arc as a Day-1 Launch Partner
summary: Frankfurt, New York, 1st October 2026, Chainwire
content:

Frankfurt, New York, 1st October 2026, Chainwire

Frankfurt, New York, October 1st, 2026, Chainwire

Partnership to explore the use of Arc for tokenized securities on 21X Group’s trading and settlement systems

21X Group, whose subsidiary 21X AG operates the first fully regulated trading and settlement system for tokenized securities in the EU, today announced that it has been named a Day-1 launch partner in the Arc ecosystem as the network moves to public mainnet in the EU and US. 21X Group and Circle have entered into a collaboration to build use cases for issuers and brokers of tokenized securities on Arc across EU and US markets.

Arc is an open, EVM-compatible Layer-1 blockchain built for the world’s financial markets, real-time money movement and agentic economic activity. It uses stablecoins as gas, starting with Circle’s own USDC.

In the EU, 21X AG operates a venue where institutional participants can issue, trade and settle tokenized securities through atomic delivery versus payment, reducing settlement time and principal risk. Its European venue currently supports USDC as a settlement currency.

21X LLC announced its anticipated entry into the US on the 29th of September 2026 in a move into the world’s largest capital market, which marks its first expansion outside Europe. 21X LLC is seeking US regulatory approvals to form a US broker-dealer that will operate an alternative trading system that will offer subscribers the ability to trade in tokenized securities.

Within the collaboration, 21X Group and Circle are exploring Arc as a network for the issuance, trading and settlement of tokenized securities in the EU and US. Ahead of the Arc mainnet launch, the two companies successfully tested the trading of tokenized securities on Arc through 21X AG’s EU capital market infrastructure – leveraging atomic settlement against USDC in under one second.

Asset managers in the Arc ecosystem will be able to work with 21X AG’s existing EU platform and expected US platform, pending both EU and US regulatory approvals, to list tokenized securities on Arc to enable trading against USDC. Building on their existing collaboration in Europe, the companies are further exploring how Circle’s broader infrastructure can support institutional access to stablecoins while enabling cross-chain interoperability for USDC.

Max Heinzle, Founder and CEO, 21X Group, said: “Arc is purpose-built for financial applications and offers a natural environment for stablecoins and tokenized securities operations. Exploring 21X LLC’s anticipated trading and settlement capabilities on Arc will allow us to build on what we have already established in Europe, where participants can settle tokenized securities against USDC through atomic delivery versus payment. We are pleased to join the Arc ecosystem from day one.”

Ray Tierney, CEO, 21X LLC, added: “The US is the world’s largest capital market, and will be central to the next phase of tokenization. As we build out 21X LLC’s US operation, our focus is on creating regulated institutional access to tokenized securities across open blockchain networks. Joining the Arc ecosystem from day one is an important step in that strategy.”

About 21X Group

21X Group is an international financial market infrastructure group building regulated, tokenized capital markets, comprising 21X AG and 21X Service GmbH in Europe; and 21X LLC and 21X USA LLC in the United States.

On September 8, 2025, 21X AG opened the first authorized distributed ledger technology trading and settlement system (DLT TSS) in the EU, positioning the company as a leader in the transition from traditional to tokenized asset-based capital markets.

21X AG operates its trading and settlement venue in the EU under BaFin (Bundesanstalt für Finanzdienstleistungsaufsicht) and ESMA (European Securities and Markets Authority) oversight. Its infrastructure is designed to operate across multiple distributed ledger networks, adapted to the regulatory requirements of the markets in which it operates. 21X AG’s platform in the EU enables atomic trading without counterparty risk through smart contract-based issuance, trading and settlement of tokenized stocks, bonds and funds.

See the video about 21X Group and our blockchain-based exchange here.

Important information

21X LLC is not a registered broker-dealer under the U.S. Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended and under applicable state laws in the United States or a member of the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Inc. Accordingly, this press release and its contents do not constitute an offer or invitation to sell, purchase or subscribe for, any securities or any other banking, investment, insurance or other product or service to US Persons (as such term is defined in the federal securities laws of the United States). This communication was reviewed by FINRA.

About Circle

Circle (NYSE: CRCL) is one of the world’s leading internet financial platform companies, building the foundation of a more open, global economy through programmable blockchain infrastructure, digital assets, and payment applications. Circle’s platform includes the world’s largest stablecoin network anchored by USDC, Circle Payments Network for global money movement, and Arc, an enterprise-grade blockchain designed to become the Economic OS for the internet. Enterprises, financial institutions, and developers use Circle to power trusted, internet-scale financial innovation.

title: Crypto for Advisors: The CLARITY Act failed, but the rules came anyway
content:
Oct 1, 2026, 11:00 a.m. EDT

6 min read

Summary

Happy Thursday, advisors!

In today’s newsletter, Alex Tapscott of CMCC Global Capital Markets on the rules regulators are writing while Congress stalls, and how long that can hold.

Then, in “Ask an Expert,” Leo Mindyuk of ML Tech on what a client owns when they buy a tokenized stock.

Happy reading.

The CLARITY Act failed. Regulatory clarity arrived anyway.

Regulators have provided what Congress could not, providing a short-term boost and creating a longer-term risk.

On Sept. 15, the U.S. Senate had a chance to take a major step toward setting the rules of the road for digital assets and, by extension, the digital economy we are now entering.

It didn’t.

The CLARITY Act failed to advance, meaning a comprehensive legislated framework for digital assets — including tokenized money, stocks, bonds, deeds and other assets — and the exchanges, brokers, issuers and intermediaries that deal in them would have to wait.

CLARITY would have strengthened American leadership, benefited the American consumer and, as I argued in CoinDesk not long ago, given banks and other legacy enterprises a clear path to invest, build, compete — and perhaps even win the future of financial services.

There is nothing so powerful as an idea whose time has come. For now, that time has not arrived. But as Congress closed a door, regulators opened a window.

Both the SEC and CFTC moved with remarkable speed. Just two days after CLARITY failed, the SEC issued an “Innovation Exemption” allowing certain venues to trade tokenized U.S.-listed stocks onchain using automated market makers and liquidity pools. Chairman Paul Atkins called it a “bridge toward durable rulemaking.”

The CFTC has also been stripping away practical barriers, providing relief to certain software providers and updating guidance around tokenized investments and blockchain-based recordkeeping.

Congress declined to build the bridge, so regulators like Atkins have started laying planks themselves.

The question now is whether regulatory clarity can substitute for legislative clarity — and, if so, for how long.

Perhaps regulators recognize something Congress has yet to fully accommodate: the genie is already out of the bottle.

New technologies generally need three things to achieve mass adoption: technology that works, products people want and a regulatory environment that allows companies to build. Crypto increasingly has the first two. Regulators are now attempting to provide the third.

The technology is ready for prime time. Solana, for example, can handle the same transaction volume as the equity, fixed-income and foreign exchange markets combined. Platforms like Hyperliquid, which provide real-time, 24/7/365 trading in virtually any market, are beginning to eat into traditional commodities futures markets.

There is also clear product-market fit. Stablecoins are crypto’s first killer app, but they won’t be its last. Once the world gets its hands on digital money, the next thing people will want is a way to save, earn and invest with that money. Tokenized stocks and bonds, along with convenient and easy-to-access onchain markets, will fill that role, and we haven’t even discussed the explosive upside of agentic commerce happening with digital assets.

The missing ingredient to unleash this capability truly has been regulatory clarity.

CLARITY was supposed to be the watershed: the moment crypto companies, banks and others could compete on a level playing field, knowing the rules of the road.

Can regulators fill that gap?

Perhaps, at least for now.

But there is an important difference between regulatory permission and legislative certainty. Regulators can tell companies what they may do today. Legislation provides greater protection against a future administration deciding something different tomorrow.

That distinction matters enormously to a bank, exchange or asset manager committing billions of dollars to infrastructure that may take a decade to pay off.

The future, however, is not something to be predicted. It is something to be achieved.

The key question is how much work can get done in the next two years.

This is an opportunity for the industry to create facts on the ground: products consumers actually use, infrastructure financial institutions depend upon, businesses that employ people and invest capital, and markets that demonstrably work better than what came before.

The deeper blockchain becomes embedded in the productive economy, the harder it will be for any future government — Democratic or Republican — to justify turning back the clock.

That opportunity could still be squandered. If the crypto industry spends this window chasing the same short-term gains that defined past cycles or continues to politicize the technology and alienate those with whom it disagrees, a historic economic opportunity could be lost.

Stripe, Circle, Robinhood and other innovators are unlikely to wait. Incumbent financial institutions face a harder choice: wait for Congress to provide the certainty they would prefer or move under the certainty regulators can provide currently.

Waiting may feel prudent. It may prove considerably riskier.

CLARITY didn’t happen. But clarity, of a sort, is emerging anyway.

The window is open. The industry should push through as many useful innovations and products as it can.

- Alex Tapscott, CEO, CMCC Global Capital Markets

Ask an Expert

Q: What does the SEC's five-year "Innovation Exemption" change after CLARITY stalled?

A: The SEC has opened a pathway for eligible tokenized U.S.-listed stocks to trade onchain through automated liquidity pools. Qualifying venues don't have to register as exchanges, and certain liquidity providers receive dealer-registration relief for covered activities. Trading is limited to identity-verified participants. The order followed CLARITY’s failed procedural Senate vote by two days. Its scope is narrower than the proposed legislation, which also addresses tokenized securities. It allows a specific market model to develop under existing SEC authority.

It's also a deliberately limited test. Trading is capped at a small fraction of each stock's normal volume, and margin isn't allowed. The relief lasts five years, but the SEC can modify its terms or duration.

Advisors should treat this as a limited market test and require evidence that a product improves access or execution at their clients’ actual trade sizes.

Q: If a client buys a “tokenized stock,” what do they actually own?

A: Some products marketed as “tokenized stocks” provide synthetic exposure to a stock’s returns without conveying shareholder rights. Payments that mirror dividends don't make the holder a shareholder. The SEC's new exemption sets a useful test. To trade on these venues, a token has to carry the same rights as the underlying share: the same dividends, the same votes and the same claim on the company's assets in a liquidation. Synthetic exposure doesn't qualify. If a third party tokenizes a company's stock without the company's involvement, it has to deliver proxy materials to holders. The company also gets 30 days' notice and can block trading on that venue.

Advisors should read the documents that set out the client's rights. Check how dividends and votes actually reach the client. Identify whether the token represents direct ownership, an indirect interest in shares held in custody or a contractual claim tied to the stock’s returns. Most important, find out what the client can claim if the tokenization provider fails. Is the client recorded as a shareholder with the transfer agent, or do they hold a claim against a custodian or a special-purpose vehicle?

Q: After verifying the rights, what should advisors test before allocating?

A: I would compare the tokenized share with the conventional share at the client’s actual trade size, including fees and price impact. Check price deviations from the conventional share during stress. In a liquidity pool, the displayed price is only a starting point: an order can move the price by changing the pool’s asset balances. Who supplies that liquidity, and can they keep doing so during volatility?

Then examine custody, transfer restrictions and the documented exit process if a venue closes or the tokenization arrangement ends. Require evidence of a specific benefit. For example, better access, lower total trading costs or settlement that makes funds available sooner. Those benefits should justify the added operational risk and fit the client’s investment objectives.

- Leo Mindyuk, CEO, ML Tech

title: NEAR Intents hit by $3.8 million exploit as crypto's rough year of hacks continues
summary: The popular cross-chain trading system said it will reimburse losses after a bug affected deposits and withdrawals across several networks.
content:
Oct 1, 2026, 10:18 a.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • NEAR Intents suffered a security exploit Thursday that caused about $3.8 million in losses and prompted the cross-chain trading platform to pause services and restrict deposits and withdrawals on several blockchains.
  • The project attributed the exploit to a bug involving its Omni system and smart contract, said the vulnerability had been patched and pledged to reimburse affected funds in full.
  • NEAR Intents reported the incident to law enforcement and enlisted security firms to trace funds that an investigator said were sent to KuCoin and converted into bitcoin.

Blockchain protocol NEAR Intents was hit by a security exploit that caused about $3.8 million in losses Thursday, forcing the platform to pause services and temporarily disable deposits and withdrawals on several blockchains.

The project said the incident was caused by a bug in the way its Omni deposit and withdrawal system interacted with the NEAR Intents smart contract. The contract-side vulnerability has since been patched, and NEAR Intents said affected funds will be reimbursed in full.

NEAR Intents is designed to make cross-chain trading simpler. Instead of asking users to choose a bridge, exchange or route themselves, they specify the swap they want and independent market makers, known as solvers, compete to complete it behind the scenes. The platform’s website said it has processed more than $30 billion in volume across 35 blockchains.

NEAR NEAR$4.9364, the native token of the blockchain closely associated with NEAR Intents, was down about 6% over the past 24 hours at the time of writing, though the disclosed vulnerability involved its cross-chain infrastructure rather than the underlying NEAR Protocol blockchain.

The incident adds to a rough year for crypto security. Just last week, exchange Bitget suffered an exploit that resulted in over $350 million in stolen assets. Other major incidents included Liquid Network at about $320 million, Drift at $295 million and Kelp at $293 million, according to DefiLlama data.

NEAR Intents said it reported the incident to law enforcement and is working with security and blockchain analytics firms to trace the funds.

Blockchain investigator ZachXBT said the exploit began with irregular withdrawals from a BNB Chain hot wallet linked to NEAR Intents. He said the stolen funds were then sent to crypto exchange KuCoin and bridged into bitcoin BTC$84,942.12.

The platform expected core services to resume quickly, but deposits and withdrawals on several networks were set to remain unavailable for longer while fixes were completed. Its status page showed issues affecting BNB Smart Chain, Polygon, TON, Optimism, Avalanche, Stellar, Monad, X Layer, ADI, Scroll and Plasma.

Road Town, British Virgin Islands, October 1st, 2026, Chainwire

This announcement contains inside information within the meaning of Article 87 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 (MiCA). Issuer: The Sweat Foundation Ltd, company no. 2081818, British Virgin Islands. Person making the notification: Nikolay Vznuzdaev, Director. Subject: the end of Sweat Wallet and the SWEAT Token in their Present Form on 30 December 2026.

Date and time of publication: 1 October 2026, 15:00 London time (16:00 CEST).

The Sweat Foundation Ltd (the “Foundation”) announces that Sweat Wallet and SWEAT in their present form will end on 30 December 2026. Until then the app keeps working and users keep earning. The Foundation is announcing this 90 days ahead so that every user and token holder has time to act. Details and FAQs are at https://update.swe.at

About This Announcement

Sweat Wallet and SWEAT brought more than 22 million people into Web3 through their daily steps. The economics of the current model have not held: a prolonged downturn in crypto markets, the loss of exchange listings for SWEAT, the cost of the security incident of April 2026, after which all user balances were restored, and slowing growth in new users. The team came close to sustainable profitability but did not get there. It was decided to end the current model in an orderly way, with 90 days’ notice rather than the 14 days the Foundation’s terms allow.

This announcement concerns only the Foundation’s products, Sweat Wallet and the SWEAT token. Sweatcoin is a health and wellness app operated by a separate company, Sweatco Ltd, which confirmed to the Foundation that Sweatcoin will continue to operate as normal.

An Important Update

Until 30 December 2026 the app, the token and the smart contracts keep running as today, and users keep earning for as long as movement verification data is supplied by Sweatcoin. The minimum term on Grow Jars is removed no later than 15 October 2026.

After 30 December 2026 the app and the services around it end in their present form. The SWEAT token continues to exist on NEAR and on the EVM chains where it is bridged. When the Foundation closes the claim and Grow Jar contracts, after 30 December 2026, any unclaimed SWEAT and any Grow Jar balance, with yield calculated as of 30 December 2026, is sent to the NEAR account that owns it. The Foundation will publish in the first week of December 2026 what happens after 30 December 2026, and when.

Steps to Take Before 30 December 2026

Back up the private key and NEAR account ID from the app. Claim earned SWEAT. Withdraw from Grow Jars when preferred. Move any balances on Ethereum, Base, BSC, or Arbitrum to another wallet under your control, or bridge them to your own NEAR account while the app is running. The Foundation recommends completing these steps by 18 December 2026. Each step is explained at https://update.swe.at

The Foundation will never ask for a private key or seed phrase and will never contact users first by direct message.

Statements

Oleg Fomenko, CEO of The Sweat Foundation: “I am proud of what SWEAT achieved. Rewarding verified movement got millions of people to move more, and it brought millions of them into Web3 for the first time. That we did not reach sustainable profitability is a real disappointment to me. We are telling the community now, in full and with 90 days, because that is what our users and token holders deserve. I thank everyone who has been part of this over the last four years.”

Anton Derlyatka, CEO of Sweatco Ltd (Operator of Sweatcoin): “We thank The Sweat Foundation for the partnership that gave Sweatcoin users the chance to earn SWEAT since 2022. We’ll continue pointing our users to the Foundation’s guidance on next steps through the transition. Sweatcoin continues to help our users build healthy habits and we look forward to sharing a few new health-focused strategic partnerships in Q4.”

Notes to Editors

The Foundation has today notified a modified crypto-asset white paper for SWEAT to the Central Bank of Ireland under Article 12 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 (MiCA); the modified white paper will be published at whitepaper.swe.at/mica-compliant-white-paper on 12 October 2026.

The Sweat Foundation Ltd is registered in the British Virgin Islands (no. 2081818). Sweat Wallet is a non-custodial wallet on the NEAR Protocol with support for Ethereum, BSC, Base and Arbitrum through Chain Signatures. SWEAT is the token issued by the Foundation and minted for verified physical movement.

title: BNB Price Prediction: BNB Tests $770 Resistance as 10-Year Trendline Signals Potential Breakout
summary: BNB is trading near $770 after recovering from the $750–$760 support area, placing the token at a key technical level as traders watch resistance around $770–$775.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BNB

BNB is trading near $770 after recovering from the $750–$760 support area, placing the token at a key technical level as traders watch resistance around $770–$775.

The recent price action comes as BNB approaches a long-term ascending trendline that has been tested several times since 2018. The latest interaction occurred near $780 in September 2026, adding a longer-term technical reference to the current market structure.

BNB Price Tests $770–$775 Resistance

BNB was trading around $768–$770 on October 1, following a rebound from levels below $760. The recovery has brought the cryptocurrency back toward a resistance zone that has repeatedly attracted selling pressure in recent sessions.

BNB remains within an ascending channel but shows weakening momentum, trading near $760 below the key $770–$775 resistance zone after forming lower highs. Source: @Cryptorphic1 via X

Crypto analyst Cryptorphic1 identified an ascending channel on the 4-hour chart. According to the analysis, momentum has weakened following a rejection from the upper portion of the channel, while the formation of lower highs has kept the short-term structure under pressure.

The $770–$775 region is therefore an important area for the current BNB price action. A sustained move above it would put the upper part of the recent range back into focus, while a rejection could send the price toward the lower boundary of the ascending channel.

BNB Holds Key $750–$760 Support

The area between $750 and $760 has emerged as an important support zone during the latest consolidation. BNB recently rebounded from below $760 and subsequently reclaimed the level, indicating that buyers have remained active around the lower end of the range.

BNB trades near $770, consolidating above the $750–$760 support zone, where a strong reaction could provide another bullish opportunity. Source: @PhilippSanger62 via X

Trader @PhilippSanger62 highlighted the same support region in a September 30 analysis, noting that the price was holding above $750–$760 while trading close to $770. The accompanying 4-hour Binance chart showed the support area as a series of highlighted zones beneath the current price.

Trader @CopySkylerBFX also pointed to the $760 level after the price recovered above it on September 30. The analysis identified the previous high around $807 as a potential liquidity area if the support level continues to hold.

BNB price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

These levels provide a relatively clear framework for the near-term BNB price prediction. The $750–$760 area represents the primary downside reference, while $770–$775 remains the immediate resistance zone.

10-Year BNB Trendline Draws Attention

A separate technical setup has placed BNB’s longer-term price structure under scrutiny.

Analyst @el_crypto_prof highlighted an ascending trendline extending across nearly a decade on a two-week BNB chart. The trendline was previously tested in 2018 and 2020 before significant upward moves followed. The price returned to the broader trendline area in September 2026, with the latest interaction occurring near $780.

BNB’s 2W chart shows a nearly 10-year ascending trendline tested in 2018, 2020, and again near $780 in September 2026, with prior tests preceding major altcoin rallies. Source: @el_crypto_prof via X

The repeated historical touches are notable from a chart-structure perspective, although past reactions do not establish that the same outcome will occur again.

The analyst’s interpretation is that the latest test could coincide with renewed strength across the altcoin market. That view is based primarily on the historical behavior visible on the long-term chart rather than a confirmed change in market trend.

BNB Price Prediction: What the Chart Shows

BNB’s current setup combines a short-term resistance test with a longer-term support structure. On the 4-hour chart, the token remains inside an ascending channel but has recently shown weaker momentum after failing to maintain its move toward the upper boundary.

BNB rebounded above $760 on September 30, 2026, with the chart indicating potential continuation toward the $807 liquidity zone if support holds. Source: @CopySkylerBFX via X

A break above $770–$775 would place greater emphasis on the recent high and the $807 area identified by @CopySkylerBFX. However, such a move would need to be sustained to confirm that buyers have overcome the nearby resistance.

Conversely, a decline below $750–$760 would weaken the current rebound structure and shift attention toward the lower trendline of the ascending channel. That would also invalidate the immediate support scenario highlighted in the recent technical analyses.

For now, BNB remains caught between established support around $750–$760 and resistance near $770–$775. The reaction at these levels could provide a clearer indication of whether the current consolidation develops into another upward move or a deeper retracement.

title: Live updates: Bitcoin posts tentative gains as rates drop ahead of Friday's jobs report
summary: The euro is losing ground versus the greenback as spiking French bond yields revive memories of the European sovereign debt crisis.
content:
coverage endedOct 1, 2026, 5:00 p.m. EDT

The euro is losing ground versus the greenback as spiking French bond yields revive memories of the European sovereign debt crisis.

Fed's Jefferson says 'more time' needed before decision on additional rate hikes

“Since our September meeting, yields across the term structure have increased further, a sign that investors are reassessing the evolving macroeconomic landscape,” said Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson in prepared remarks Thursday afternoon.

“My colleagues and I will need to come to our own judgment, which may take more time,” he continued.

It’s the latest sign from the Fed that markets may have gotten ahead of themselves in assessing the pace of central bank rate hikes.

The odds of a Fed move at its Oct. 28 meeting have fallen to 30% from 70% earlier this week. And the odds of one or more rate hikes by year-end have dipped to 80% from 95% one week ago.

Bitcoin tentatively rises as rates retreat

Bitcoin BTC$84,942.12 is moving up just a bit in U.S. afternoon action, now higher by 1% over the past 24 hours at $84,800.

Possibly helping the bid is a sharp decline in interest rates on Thursday, with the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield lower by 9.4 basis points to 5.217%. Earlier in the session, it had risen to 5.36%.

The 2-year Treasury note — because of its shorter duration, more closely tied to Fed policy — is down 12.3 basis points to 4.764% as traders pare bets on additional central bank rate hikes.

Economic news released today — jobless claims and the national PMI — gave zero signs that either the economy or price pressures were easing.

At work is likely 1) satiated bond shorts lightening up ahead of tomorrow’s key U.S. September employment report, and 2) rumblings of a budding European debt crisis as French bond spreads relative to German blow out to levels not seen since the last debt crisis more than a decade ago.

Oil jumps to session high on signs of escalation in Middle East

Citing a U.S. official, the Jerusalem Post is reporting that the Trump administration is sending a third aircraft carrier and an additional Marine unit to the Middle East.

Down earlier to below $89 per barrel, WTI crude oil is now higher by 2.5% to $92.63. Brent crude is up 3.6% to $101.53.

Something breaking? French bond market teeters

“It’s been a while since we had a European sovereign debt crisis,” wrote ZeroHedge on Thursday.

Something is going on in France, where that country’s 10-year government bond (OAT) yield is up another eight basis points today, even as the German 10-year Bund yield is lower by six basis points.

That’s widened the spread between German and French 10-year paper to 135 basis points, with credit default swap (CDS) spreads on French bonds soaring to a 13-year high.

For perspective, the 10-year Bund/OAT spread has been mostly in a range of about 50-80 basis points over the past few years.

The euro is quickly losing ground versus the greenback, down another 0.9% today to $1.1231, its weakest level in about five months.

It’s a well-known axiom that central banks tighten monetary policy until something breaks, and that could be happening across the pond.

Traders continue to quickly abandon bets on another imminent Fed rate hike. The 2-year U.S. Treasury yield is down 7.5 basis points on Thursday to 4.81%, with the odds of a Fed move in October shrinking to 33.8% after sitting at about 70% earlier this week.

U.S. Manufacturing PMI meets estimates as price pressures worsen

The ISM Manufacturing PMI edged down to 54.5 in September, from 54.6 previously. Economist forecasts had been for a small rise to 55.

Any number above 50 indicates economic expansion.

The New Orders subindex rose to 55.3 from 53.7.

The Prices Paid subindex rose to 77.9 from 71.1, topping forecasts for 72.3. Perhaps even more troubling, survey respondents reported every single commodity as up in price and exactly zero commodities as down in price.

Bottom line: The report shows an economy still in strong expansion mode with inflation pressures worsening.

Markets aren’t really reacting as traders look ahead to tomorrow’s September employment report.

NEAR token sinks 9% on reported exploit

According to crypto-sleuth ZachXBT, NEAR Intents was exploited for $3.8 million several hours ago.

NEAR Intents has reportedly temporarily suspended operations.

NEAR token is lower by 9%.

Update: “Earlier today NEAR Intents services were stopped after a security incident was detected,” wrote the NEAR Intents team. “The incident was caused by a bug in the Omni deposit and withdrawal infrastructure interaction with NEAR Intents smart contract.”

“The contract-side vulnerability has been patched. The operations of the NEAR Intents and near(.)com are expected to resume within 1h.”

Monthly move in bond yields was largest in four years

The 10-year Treasury yield rose by a whopping 53 basis points in September, the largest monthly move since September 2022, according to Yahoo Finance’s Julie Hyman.

She noted that the big move in yields in September 2022 was enough to knock the S&P 500 down by more than 9% that month. This time around, though, stocks barely budged, the S&P 500 dipping just 0.45%.

As for bitcoin, it fell 3.1% in September 2022 — actually not too bad a result considering the carnage in crypto that year. BTC rose 6.3% this past September.

Jobless claims continue to show no stress in labor market

Initial jobless claims edged lower to 197,000 last week, according to a just-released government report. That’s down from 198,000 previously and just below market forecasts for 200,000.

The four-week average dipped to 200,000 from 202,500.

Twenty-four hours from now, markets will get the government’s Nonfarm Payrolls Report for September, with economists expecting 90,000 jobs to have been added and the unemployment rate to hold at 4.1%.

Bitcoin treading water as fourth quarter gets underway

Bitcoin BTC$84,942.12 rose 42.7% in the third quarter, its best quarterly performance since jumping 68.7% in the first quarter of 2024. Ether ETH$2,710.86 rose 70.8%, its best result since soaring 160.7% in the first quarter of 2021.

Both cryptos are about flat on the first day of the fourth quarter, with bitcoin just under $84,000 and ether just above $2,700.

Interest rates have become the big macro story, with the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield touching yet another 24-year high overnight at 5.362%. It’s since pulled back to 5.282% as bearish traders likely hedge bets ahead of tomorrow’s U.S. Nonfarm Payrolls Report for September.

Economist forecasts are for the U.S. to have added 90,000 jobs last month and the unemployment rate to hold at 4.1%.
